---
title: Images, icons and fonts
description: Network and asset images, icon constants, and adding fonts and files to the app
---

## Images

Images are Flutter's `Image`. Its named constructors are components of their own:

```tsx
import { ImageNetwork, ImageAsset } from "#fuse/flutter";

<ImageNetwork src="https://example.com/cat.jpg" width={120} height={120} fit="cover" />
<ImageAsset name="assets/logo.png" width={48} />
```

`fit` is Flutter's `BoxFit`: `"cover"`, `"contain"`, `"fill"`... Round the corners by clipping the box around it:

```tsx
<View decoration={{ borderRadius: 12 }} clipBehavior="antiAlias">
  <ImageNetwork src={url()} fit="cover" />
</View>
```

`loadingBuilder` and `errorBuilder` return what to show meanwhile and on failure.

A design package brings `Image`. In an app without one, add it to `dart/lib/fuse.dart` first: see [All of Flutter from JSX](/docs/flutter/widgets#what-crosses).

## Assets

Files that ship with the app are Flutter assets. List them in `dart/pubspec.yaml`, with paths from `dart/`:

```yaml title="dart/pubspec.yaml"
flutter:
  assets:
    - assets/js/        # the app's bundle: keep this line
    - assets/logo.png
```

## Fonts

Fonts are declared the same way, then named in `fontFamily`:

```yaml title="dart/pubspec.yaml"
flutter:
  fonts:
    - family: Inter
      fonts:
        - asset: assets/fonts/Inter-Regular.ttf
        - asset: assets/fonts/Inter-Bold.ttf
          weight: 700
```

```tsx
<Text fontFamily="Inter" fontWeight={700}>Hello</Text>
```

To use it everywhere, set it on the app root: `theme={{ fontFamily: "Inter" }}` on `MaterialApp`, `textStyle={{ fontFamily: "Inter" }}` on core's `App`.

Restart the app after changing `pubspec.yaml`.

## Icons

`Icon` draws one glyph. Its `icon` is a constant from a design package: `Icons` from `@solid-fuse/material`, `CupertinoIcons` from `@solid-fuse/cupertino`. The names are Flutter's.

```tsx
import { Icon } from "solid-fuse";
import { Icons } from "@solid-fuse/material";

<Icon icon={Icons.search} size={24} color="#111827" />
```

```tsx
import { CupertinoIcons } from "@solid-fuse/cupertino";

<Icon icon={CupertinoIcons.heart} />
```

An icon constant is the Dart constant's name (`"Icons.search"`), not a code point. The bundle keeps only the icons it uses, and `fuse build` keeps only their Dart side, so Flutter's icon tree shaking keeps working: the app ships the glyphs it uses, not the whole font.

### Reactive props

Every prop is reactive.

```tsx
const [liked, setLiked] = createSignal(false);

<Icon icon={liked() ? Icons.favorite : Icons.favorite_border} color={liked() ? "#EF4444" : "#6B7280"} />
```

### Icons in other widgets

The design packages' slots that take an icon (`leading`, `prefixIcon`, a button's `icon`) take the constant itself, or any element:

```tsx
<TextField label="Search" prefixIcon={Icons.search} />
<ListTile leading={<Icon icon={Icons.wifi} color="#16A34A" />} title="Wi-Fi" />
```

### Lucide

`@solid-fuse/lucide` wraps the [`flutter_lucide`](https://pub.dev/packages/flutter_lucide) font. Add it to `package.json` and run `fuse link`.

```tsx
import { LucideIcons } from "@solid-fuse/lucide";

<Icon icon={LucideIcons.heart} />
```

### Your own icon font

Export your icons from your app's `dart/lib/fuse.dart` as a class of `IconData` constants; [generation](/docs/flutter/widgets) turns them into constants like `Icons`. To share one as a package, copy `packages/lucide`: it is a `fuse.dart` with one `export ... show` line and an `index.ts` that re-exports the generated class.

Props: [Icon](/docs/reference/components#icon).
